engraved with the words: AUTHORITY MUST BE ACCEPTED.

has a conspicuously empty socket for a counterweight.

unfinished casting. Each blow throws sparks upwards into the sea.

assets.title: Greyhaven Market
assets.narration:
Greyhaven is built on a wall of pale stone above a tidal basin. Fishmongers have
abandoned their stalls to stack sandbags around the market well. A brass tide gauge
stands between them, its pointer trembling in the red.

Across the basin, rooftops emerge from the water like the backs of sleeping animals.
The old district has been submerged for sixty years. This morning, smoke is rising
from one of its chimneys.

the tide.

assets.title: The Three-Piston Hall
assets.narration:
Three great pistons rise and fall beneath a ceiling of water. One labours alone while
the other two knock uselessly against their housings. Their combined rhythm resembles
someone limping upstairs.

A maintenance board carries a diagram of the bypass circuit. Beside it hangs a
handwheel too heavy for one person to hold in place without a locking pin.

Her name, Mercy, is painted on the stern in letters someone has repaired every year.

side.

faded instruction reads: THREE LONG FLASHES. KEEP THE SOUTH CHANNEL CLEAR.

not asking. I can change one of those today."

book he has kept dry beneath his coat.

assets.title: A Place for Every Passenger
assets.narration:

lower city, too. If you find someone below, send them there. If the signal tower
flashes three times, I will clear the south channel and stay there."

assets.title: Four Ways to End a Watch
assets.narration:
"You can correct the account," Hester says. "Bring the names from the memorial and a
witnessed promise from the people above. The engine can sustain shared work. It will
release those entered without consent."

"You can take my place voluntarily. The wall will stand, but you will remain here. You
can also evacuate through the controlled spillway, if Mercy is ready and the beacon is
lit. The city will be lost gradually enough for its people to leave."

"Or you can break the engine. With the ferry and signal prepared, people can escape
the surge, though their homes cannot. Without them, the flood will take the crowded
quay. I will not call that an accident."

She gives you her authority plate. "The auditor in the heart vault will recognise
this. You may still return to the square before committing yourself."

assets.title: The Engineer Who Could Not Stop the Gate
assets.narration:
"I designed a wall that needed maintenance," Hester says. "The council wanted one that
needed obedience. When the storm came, they opened the gates before the last boat
returned. Then they gave the engine the names of the people they had killed."

"I stayed to keep the pressure from crushing them. I told myself I could repair the
account next week. Then next year. I have held it long enough for my daughter to
become an old woman."

She touches the restrained clapper. "I was useful. Being useful made it easy to
postpone being right. Do not inherit that excuse with my office."

assets.title: What It Means to Close an Account
assets.narration:
Hester's notes describe an older agreement. The wall was sustained by voluntary work:
watchkeepers, repairs, shared stores. The emergency council replaced those
contributions with the names of people it had failed to evacuate. The engine cannot
distinguish a promise from a debt entered in an official ledger.

To release the dead without dropping the wall, someone must stabilise the pumps, fit a
new weight and carry a witnessed correction into the heart vault. The correction must
name the people removed from the public account. The people above must accept the work
that was stolen from them.

The refuge holds survivors and descendants. The memorial supplies the names. The
keeper at the tidal bell can open the heart vault, but Hester warned against accepting
her office before understanding its price.

assets.title: A Tide That Has Forgotten Its Hour
assets.narration:
The tide gauge rings once, then falls silent with its pointer still climbing. A young

assets.title: The Ferry Beneath the Crane
assets.narration:
An older ferryman is lying flat on the quay, reaching for a rope just beyond his
fingertips. People on the warehouse roof are keeping very still. The incoming water is
already touching the lowest tiles.

"Bram," he says when you kneel beside him. "I have run Mercy through worse weather.
Never thought I would lose her in her own berth. Get the crane off her and I can take
these people to Lantern Island."

He has a sound plan: secure the crane to a bollard, then work the warehouse winch. It
will take patience, not heroics.

needing anyone again." Once you sign, the dead will be free to leave the engine.

are also leaving work unfinished."

assets.title: Turn the Memorial Face Up
assets.narration:

time. Beneath the dried mud are names, occupations and ages. Nobody has been described

bottom, a line reads: THE WATER WAS OPENED BEFORE THE LAST BOAT RETURNED.

A small brass nameplate has survived beside the stone. It belonged to a house rather
than a grave.

assets.title: The Harbour in Miniature

says. He died maintaining a clear channel. He has not noticed that his orders have
become the obstruction.

assets.title: The Surveyor's Commission
assets.narration:
Ivo spreads his chart across an empty fish stall. Sixty years ago, Greyhaven flooded
its lower district to relieve a winter storm. Afterwards, an engine beneath the sea
wall kept the upper city safe. The official account says Lowwater was empty when the
gates opened.

"The engine is losing pressure. I need someone to reset the pumps, replace a broken
counterweight and recover the original maintenance ledger. The ledger will tell us how
to close the account."

He points to the lockhouse. "The inspection stair is dry. Beyond it, I cannot promise
anything. Captain Venn has the survey seal. People on the quay need help, too. I would
rather lose a day than pretend they are cargo."

I am less certain that makes them good orders."

assets.title: Hear the People Left Off the Account
assets.narration:
You lay the original ledger on the long table. Sella reads the first page, then asks
the room to keep quiet while the people from Lowwater speak.

A cooper remembers the warning being given after the gangplanks were raised. A
laundress remembers refusing to leave a neighbour who could not walk. Sella remembers
waiting on the last boat for a mother who never arrived.

Their stories disagree in small details. They agree that nobody consented to become
part of a machine. The living at the table offer to take turns maintaining the wall,
if the stolen names can be released.
